title: Where Celsus’s phrases came from
source_text: Τὸ μὲν γὰρ χρῆσθαι προφητῶν λόγοις ἡμῶν ἐστι, τῶν παριστάντων Ἰησοῦν εἶναι τὸν προκεκηρυγμένον ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν Χριστὸν καὶ ἀποδεικνύντων ἐκ τῶν προφητικῶν τὰ ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πληρωθέντα. τὸ δὲ κύκλους ἐπὶ κύκλοις λέγειν τάχα μὲν καὶ τῆς προειρημένης ἐστὶν αἱρέσεως, κύκλῳ περιλαμβανούσης ἑνὶ, ἥν φασιν εἶναι τὴν τῶν ὅλων ψυχὴν καὶ Λευϊαθὰν, τοὺς ἑπτὰ τῶν ἀρχοντικῶν κύκλους. τάχα δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἐκκλησιαστοῦ ἐστι παράκουσμα λέγοντος· „κυκλοῖ κυκλῶν πορεύεται τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ ἐπὶ κύκλους αὐτοῦ ἐπιστρέφει τὸ πνεῦμα.“ τὸ δ᾿ ἀποῤῥοίας ἐκκλησίας ἐπιγείου καὶ περιτομῆς τάχα ἐλήφθη ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπό τινων λέγεσθαι ἐκκλησίας τινὸς ἐπουρανίου καὶ κρείττονος αἰῶνος ἀπόῤῥοιαν εἶναι τὴν ἐπὶ γῆς ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ περιτομῆς τινος ἐν καθαρσίῳ τινὶ ἐκεῖ γεγενημένης σύμβολον εἶναι τὴν ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γεγραμμένην. Προυνικὸν δέ τινα σοφίαν οἱ ἀπὸ Οὐαλεντίνου ὀνομάζουσι κατὰ τὴν πεπλανημένην ἑαυτῶν σοφίαν, ης σύμβολον εἶναι βούλονται καὶ δώδεκα ἔτεσιν αἱμοῤῥοοῦσαν· ἣν παρακούσας ὁ ἅμα πάντα φύρων τὰ Ἑλλήνων καὶ βαρβάρων καὶ τῶν ἐν ταῖς αἱρέσεσιν εἶπε τό· Προυνικοῦ τινος δύναμιν ῥέουσαν παρθένου. ψυχὴ δὲ ζῶσα τάχα μὲν ἐν ἀποῤῥήτοις λέλεκται παρά τισι τῶν ἀπὸ Οὐαλεντίνου εἰς τὸν ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν ὀνομαζόμενον „ψυχικὸν δημιουργὸν,“ τάχα δὲ καὶ πρὸς ἀντιδιαστολὴν ψυχῆς νεκρᾶς ἡ ζῶσα ψυχὴ οὐκ ἀγεννῶς παρά τισι λέλεκται ἡ τοῦ σῳζομένου. σφαζόμενον δ᾿ οὐκ οἶδα οὐρανὸν λελεγμένον ἢ γῆν σφαζομένην μαχαίρᾳ καὶ πολλοὺς σφαζομένους, ἵνα ζήσωσι. καὶ οὐκ ἀπεικός ἐστιν ἀφ᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ταῦτα κεκομικέναι τὸν Κέλσον.
pass_a_gloss: For to use the words of prophets is ours, who show (παριστάντων) that Jesus is the Christ proclaimed beforehand (προκεκηρυγμένον) by them, and demonstrate (ἀποδεικνύντων) from the prophetic writings the things in the Gospels about Jesus as fulfilled (πληρωθέντα). To say circles upon circles is perhaps (τάχα) of the aforesaid heresy, enclosing (περιλαμβανούσης) in one circle, which they say is the soul of the whole (τὴν τῶν ὅλων ψυχήν) and Leviathan, the seven circles of the archons. Perhaps it is a mishearing (παράκουσμα) from Ecclesiastes saying: 'Circling, circling goes the wind/spirit (κυκλοῖ κυκλῶν πορεύεται τὸ πνεῦμα), and on its circles the wind returns.' 'Emanations of an earthly church and of circumcision' was perhaps taken from its being said by some that the church on earth is an emanation (ἀπόρροιαν) of a certain heavenly church (ἐπουρανίου) and better aeon (κρείττονος αἰῶνος), and that the circumcision written in the law is a symbol (σύμβολον) of a circumcision that took place there in a certain purification (καθαρσίῳ). Those from Valentinus name a certain wisdom (σοφίαν) Prunicus according to their own wandering/erring wisdom (πεπλανημένην σοφίαν), of which they want the woman bleeding twelve years (δώδεκα ἔτεσιν αἱμορροοῦσαν) to be a symbol; mishearing which, he who mixes all at once (ἅμα πάντα φύρων) the things of Greeks and barbarians and those in heresies said: 'flowing power of a certain virgin Prunicus.' A living soul has perhaps been said in secret teachings (ἐν ἀπορρήτοις) by some from Valentinus of the one named by them 'psychic demiurge' (ψυχικὸν δημιουργόν); perhaps for distinction (ἀντιδιαστολήν) from a dead soul (ψυχῆς νεκρᾶς) the soul of the one being saved (τοῦ σῳζομένου) has been called not ignobly (οὐκ ἀγεννῶς) by some the living soul. A slaughtered heaven I do not know to have been said, nor earth slaughtered by a sword, nor many slaughtered that they may live; and it is not unlikely (οὐκ ἀπεικός) that Celsus brought (κεκομικέναι) these from himself.
pass_b_english: For to use the words of prophets is indeed our practice: we show that Jesus is the Christ proclaimed beforehand by them, and we prove from the prophetic writings that what the Gospels record about Jesus was fulfilled. To speak of “circles upon circles” perhaps belongs to the heresy mentioned before, which encloses within one circle, which they say is the soul of the universe and Leviathan, the seven circles of the archons. Or perhaps it is a mishearing of Ecclesiastes, who says: “Circling round and round the wind goes, and on its circles the wind returns” (Ecclesiastes 1:6).

“Emanations of an earthly church and of circumcision” was perhaps taken from the claim made by some that the church on earth is an emanation of a heavenly church and a higher aeon, and that the circumcision written in the law is a symbol of a circumcision performed there in a certain rite of cleansing. The followers of Valentinus give the name Prunicus to a certain Wisdom, in keeping with their own wisdom that has gone astray, and they want the woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years to be a symbol of her (Matthew 9:20; Mark 5:25; Luke 8:43). The man who jumbles together everything from Greeks and barbarians and those in the heresies misheard this and spoke of “the flowing power of a certain virgin, Prunicus”.

“A living soul” has perhaps been said in secret teachings by some of the followers of Valentinus of the one they call “the psychic demiurge”; or perhaps the soul of one who is being saved has been called, not unworthily, “the living soul” by some, to distinguish it from a dead soul. But I do not know of any talk of “a heaven slain”, or “an earth slain with a sword”, or “many slain that they may live”; and it is not unlikely that Celsus brought these in out of his own head.

choices.choice: Ecclesiastes 1:6 checked against the LXX wording (κυκλοῖ κυκλῶν πορεύεται τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ ἐπὶ κύκλους αὐτοῦ ἐπιστρέφει τὸ πνεῦμα); πνεῦμα rendered ‘wind’ as the verse’s sense, though the word also means ‘spirit’, which may be how the sect read it. The woman with the twelve-year flow of blood: no verse is quoted, but the allusion is clear; all three Synoptic passages cited. ‘Living soul’ (ψυχὴ ζῶσα) echoes Genesis 2:7 and 1 Corinthians 15:45, but Origen ties it here to Valentinian usage, not to a verse, so the echo is noted only. ψυχικὸς δημιουργός is the Valentinian technical term for the maker of the soul-endowed order (not the Creator God of 6.30), kept as ‘the psychic demiurge’, lower case. κατὰ τὴν πεπλανημένην ἑαυτῶν σοφίαν is ironic and double-edged (their Wisdom who strayed / their own misguided wisdom); ‘in keeping with their own wisdom that has gone astray’ keeps both. ὁ ἅμα πάντα φύρων is Origen’s description of Celsus; the name is not added. ‘The heresy mentioned before’ with its Leviathan circle refers to the Ophite diagram described at 6.25. Celsus’s phrases are in double quotation marks.
